title: Homily II — Today the living ark comes to rest

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, cols. 724-728 (PDF leaves 403-405)

source_text: Σήμερον ἡ ὁσία καὶ μόνη Παρθένος τῷ ὑπερκοσμίῳ καὶ οὐρανίῳ τεμένει προσάγεται, ἡ τοσοῦτον τὴν παρθενίαν ποθήσασα, ὡς ὑπ' αὐτῆς οἷά τινος καθαρωτάτου ποιωθῆναι πυρός. Παρθένος γὰρ ἅπασα τῷ τόκῳ τὴν παρθενίαν λυμαίνεται· αὕτη δὲ καὶ πρὸ τόκου, καὶ τίκτουσα μένει παρθένος, καὶ μετὰ γέννησιν. Σήμερον ἡ ἱερά τε καὶ ἔμψυχος κιβωτὸς τοῦ ζῶντος Θεοῦ, ἡ τὸν ἑαυτῆς τεχνίτην κυοφορήσασα, ἐν ναῷ Κυρίου ἀχειροτμήτῳ καταπαύεται, καὶ σκιρτᾷ Δαβὶδ ὁ ταύτης προπάτωρ καὶ Θεοπάτωρ, καὶ συγχορεύουσιν ἄγγελοι, καὶ κροτοῦσιν ἀρχάγγελοι, καὶ δυνάμεις δοξάζουσι, καὶ ἀρχαὶ συναγάλλονται, καὶ ἐξουσίαι εὐφραίνονται, καὶ κυριότητες χαίρουσιν, καὶ θρόνοι πανηγυρίζουσι, καὶ ἀνυμνεῖ τὰ Χερουβὶμ, καὶ δοξολογεῖ τὰ Σεραφίμ. Δοξάζονται γὰρ οὐχ ἥκιστα, τῇ Μητρὶ τῆς δόξης τὴν δόξαν προσνέμοντες. Σήμερον ἡ ἱερωτάτη περιστερὰ, ἡ ἀκεραία καὶ ἄκακος ψυχὴ, καὶ τῷ θείῳ καθιερωμένη Πνεύματι, ἐκπτᾶσα τῆς κιβωτοῦ, τοῦ θεοδόχου φημὶ, καὶ ζωαρχικοῦ σώματος, εὗρεν ἀνάπαυσιν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῆς, πρὸς τὸν νοητὸν κόσμον ἀπάρασα, καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀσπίλῳ γῇ τῆς ἄνω κληρουχίας σκηνώσασα. Σήμερον ἡ Ἐδὲμ τοῦ νέου Ἀδὰμ τὸν λογικὸν παράδεισον ὑποδέχεται, ἐν ᾧ τὸ κατάκριμα λέλυται, ἐν ᾧ τὸ τῆς ζωῆς ξύλον πεφύτευται, ἐν ᾧ ἡ ἡμετέρα περιέσταλται γύμνωσις. Οὐκέτι γὰρ ἡμεῖς γυμνοὶ καὶ ἀνείμονες, καὶ τῆς θείας εἰκόνος μὴ φέροντες τὴν λαμπρότητα· καὶ τὴν ἄφθονον χάριν σεσυλημένοι τοῦ Πνεύματος, οὐκέτι τὴν παλαιὰν τραγῳδοῦντες γύμνωσιν λέξομεν· Ἐξεδυσάμην τὸν χιτῶνά μου, πῶς ἐνδύσομαι αὐτόν; ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ ὁ ὄφις οὐκ ἔσχε παρείσδυσιν, οὗ τῆς ψευδοῦς ὀρεχθέντες θεώσεως, τοῖς ἀνοήτοις συμπαρεβλήθημεν κτήνεσιν. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς, Θεὸς ὢν, καὶ τῷ Πατρὶ ὁμοούσιος, ἐκ ταύτης τῆς Παρθένου καὶ καθαρᾶς ἀρούρας ἑαυτὸν πεπλαστούργηκεν ἄνθρωπον. Καὶ τεθέωμαι μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὁ θνητὸς ἠθανάτισμαι, καὶ τοὺς δερματίνους χιτῶνας ἐνδέδυμαι. Τὴν γὰρ φθορὰν ἀπημφίασμαι, περίκειμαι τῇ περιβολῇ τῆς θεότητος. Σήμερον ἡ Παρθένος ἡ ἄχραντος, καὶ γηΐνοις μὴ προσομιλήσασα πάθεσι, ἀλλ' οὐρανίοις ἐντραφεῖσα νοήμασιν, οὐκ εἰς γῆν ἀπελήλυθεν, ἀλλ' ἔμψυχος ὄντως οὐρανὸς χρηματίσασα, ταῖς οὐρανίαις σκηναῖς ἐνοικίζεται. Τίς γὰρ ταύτην οὐρανὸν καλῶν τἀληθοῦς ἁμαρτήσεται, εἰ μή πού τις φήσειε καλῶς ἐπιστάμενος, καὶ τῶν οὐρανῶν αὐτὴν ἀσυγκρίτοις ὑπεροχαῖς ὑπεραίρεσθαι. Ὁ γὰρ τῶν οὐρανῶν Δημιουργός τε καὶ Συνοχεὺς, καὶ παντὸς ἐγκοσμίου τε καὶ ὑπερκοσμίου, ὁρατοῦ τε καὶ ἀοράτου τεχνίτης δημιουργήματος, οὗ τόπος οὐδεὶς τῶν πάντων εἶναι· εἴπερ τὸ περιέχον τῶν ἐνόντων τόπος ὁρίζεται· ἐν ταύτῃ πρὸς ἑαυτοῦ ἀσπόρως βρέφος δεδημιούργηται, καὶ ταύτην ταμεῖον εὐρύχωρον δέδειχε τῆς τὰ πάντα πληρούσης αὐτοῦ καὶ μόνης ἀπεριγράφου θεότητος, ὅλος ἀπαθῶς ἐν αὐτῇ συστελλόμενος, καὶ μένων ὅλος ἐκτὸς, καὶ τόπον ἔχων ἑαυτοῦ ἀπερίληπτον. Σήμερον ὁ τῆς ζωῆς θησαυρὸς, ἡ τῆς χάριτος ἄβυσσος· οὐκ οἶδ' ὅπως τολμηροῖς καὶ ἀτρόμοις φάναι τοῖς χείλεσι· θανάτῳ ζωηφόρῳ καλύπτεται, καὶ τούτῳ ἀδειμάντως πρόσεισιν ἡ τούτου καταλύτην κυήσασα, εἰ καὶ θάνατον προσαγορεῦσαι χρεὼν τὴν αὐτῆς πανίερον καὶ ζωτικὴν ἀποβίωσιν. Ἡ γὰρ τοῖς πᾶσι τὴν ὄντως ζωὴν ἀναβλύσασα, πῶς θανάτῳ γένοιτ' ἂν ὑποχείριος· ἀλλ' εἴκει τῷ τοῦ οἰκείου τόκου θεσμοθετήματι, καὶ ὡς θυγάτηρ μὲν τοῦ πάλαι Ἀδὰμ τὰς πατρικὰς εὐθύνας ὑπερέρχεται· ἐπεὶ καὶ ὁ ταύτης Υἱὸς, ἡ αὐτοζωὴ ταύτας οὐκ ἀπηνήνατο· ὡς δὲ Θεοῦ ζῶντος μήτηρ ὑπάρξασα, πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀξίως μετακομίζεται. Εἰ γάρ φησιν ὁ Θεὸς, Μήποτε ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ὁ πρωτόπλαστος ἄνθρωπος, καὶ λαβὼν τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς, καὶ γευσάμενος, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ζήσεται, πῶς ἡ τὴν ζωὴν αὐτὴν δεξαμένη, τὴν ἄναρχόν τε καὶ ἄληκτον, τὴν μήτε ἀρχῆς, μήτε τέλους δουλεύουσαν πέρασιν, οὐκ εἰς αἰῶνα ζήσεται τὸν ἀπέραντον;
pass_a_gloss: Today the holy (ὁσία) and only Virgin (Παρθένος) is brought (προσάγεται) to the supramundane (ὑπερκοσμίῳ) and heavenly sanctuary (τέμενος), she who so longed for (ποθήσασα) virginity (παρθενία) as to be qualified/transformed (ποιωθῆναι) by it as by a most pure fire. For every virgin by birth-giving (τόκος) ruins (λυμαίνεται) virginity; but she both before birth and giving birth remains virgin, and after the begetting (γέννησις). Today the holy and ensouled (ἔμψυχος) ark (κιβωτός) of the living God, she who carried in the womb (κυοφορήσασα) her own craftsman (τεχνίτης), in a temple of the Lord not hand-cut [printed ἀχειροτμήτῳ = not made by hands] comes to rest (καταπαύεται), and David leaps (σκιρτᾷ), her forefather (προπάτωρ) and God-father/ancestor of God (Θεοπάτωρ), and angels dance together, and archangels applaud (κροτοῦσιν), and powers (δυνάμεις) glorify, and principalities (ἀρχαί) rejoice together, and authorities (ἐξουσίαι) are glad, and dominions (κυριότητες) rejoice, and thrones (θρόνοι) keep festival, and the Cherubim hymn, and the Seraphim glorify. For they are glorified not least, assigning glory to the Mother of glory. Today the most holy dove (περιστερά), the unmixed/pure (ἀκεραία) and guileless (ἄκακος) soul, consecrated to the divine Spirit, flying out from the ark, I mean the God-receiving (θεοδόχου) and life-originating (ζωαρχικοῦ) body, found rest (ἀνάπαυσιν) for her feet, departing (ἀπάρασα) to the intelligible world, and tenting (σκηνώσασα) in the spotless (ἀσπίλῳ) land of the inheritance (κληρουχία) above. Today the Eden of the new Adam receives the rational (λογικόν) paradise, in which the condemnation (κατάκριμα) has been loosed, in which the tree of life has been planted, in which our nakedness (γύμνωσις) has been wrapped. For no longer [are] we naked and unclothed (ἀνείμονες) and not bearing the brightness (λαμπρότης) of the divine image (εἰκών); and robbed (σεσυλημένοι) of the abundant grace of the Spirit, no longer, lamenting (τραγῳδοῦντες) the old nakedness, shall we say: I have taken off my tunic (χιτών), how shall I put it on? For in this the serpent (ὄφις) had no entry (παρείσδυσις), whose false deification (θέωσις) having craved (ὀρεχθέντες) we were compared with the senseless beasts (κτήνεσιν). For the only-begotten Son of God himself, being God and consubstantial (ὁμοούσιος) with the Father, from this Virgin and pure soil (ἄρουρα) formed himself a man. And I the man have been deified (τεθέωμαι), the mortal have been immortalized (ἠθανάτισμαι), and the skin garments [printed ἐνδέδυμαι 'have put on'; sense ἐκδέδυμαι 'have put off']. For I have unclothed (ἀπημφίασμαι) corruption (φθορά), I am wrapped in the robe (περιβολή) of the Godhead (θεότης). Today the immaculate Virgin, not having consorted with earthly passions but nurtured on heavenly thoughts (νοήματα), has not gone away to earth, but having become truly an ensouled heaven, is housed (ἐνοικίζεται) in the heavenly tents (σκηναί). For who calling her heaven will miss (ἁμαρτήσεται) the truth, unless someone knowing well should say she is lifted above (ὑπεραίρεσθαι) even the heavens by incomparable excellences (ὑπεροχαί). For the Creator and Sustainer (Συνοχεύς) of the heavens and craftsman of every work, within-the-world and above-the-world, visible and invisible, of whom no place of all things is [the place], if indeed place is defined as the container (τὸ περιέχον) of the things within, in her by himself seedlessly (ἀσπόρως) was fashioned an infant (βρέφος), and showed her a spacious storehouse of his all-filling and alone uncircumscribed (ἀπεριγράφου) Godhead, wholly impassibly (ἀπαθῶς) contracted in her, and remaining wholly outside, and having himself as uncontainable (ἀπερίληπτον) place. Today the treasure of life, the abyss (ἄβυσσος) of grace, I know not how to say with bold and unfearing lips, is covered by life-bearing (ζωηφόρῳ) death; and to it fearlessly (ἀδειμάντως) approaches she who conceived its destroyer (καταλύτης), if indeed one must call death her all-holy and vital departure-from-life (ἀποβίωσις). For she who gushed forth (ἀναβλύσασα) the real life for all, how could she become subject (ὑποχείριος) to death? But she yields (εἴκει) to the ordinance (θεσμοθέτημα) of her own offspring, and as daughter of the old Adam [printed ὑπερέρχεται; sense ὑπέρχεται 'undergoes'] the paternal liabilities (εὐθύνας); since also her Son, Life-itself (αὐτοζωή), did not refuse (ἀπηνήνατο) them; but as having been mother of the living God, she is worthily transported to him. For if God says: Lest stretching out his hand the first-formed (πρωτόπλαστος) man and taking of the tree of life and tasting, he will live forever, how will she who received the life itself, the beginningless (ἄναρχον) and unceasing (ἄληκτον), serving neither the bounds (πέρασιν) of beginning nor of end, not live to the endless (ἀπέραντον) age?
pass_b_english: Today the holy and only Virgin is brought to the sanctuary of heaven, beyond this world: she who so loved virginity that it transformed her, as a most pure fire would. For every virgin loses her virginity in giving birth; but she remains a virgin before giving birth, in giving birth, and after the birth. Today the holy and living ark of the living God, who carried her own Maker in her womb, comes to rest in the temple of the Lord not made by hands; and David, her forefather and the forefather of God, leaps for joy (2 Samuel 6:14–16), and angels dance with him, archangels applaud, powers give glory, principalities rejoice together, authorities are glad, dominions exult, thrones keep festival, the Cherubim sing hymns and the Seraphim give praise. For they are glorified not least by offering glory to the Mother of glory. Today the most holy dove, the pure and innocent soul consecrated to the divine Spirit, flying out from the ark, I mean the body that received God and was the beginning of life, has found rest for her feet (Genesis 8:9). She has set out for the world known to the mind, and has made her dwelling in the spotless land of the inheritance above. Today the Eden of the new Adam receives the paradise endowed with reason, in which the sentence of condemnation has been undone, in which the tree of life has been planted, in which our nakedness has been clothed. For we are no longer naked and unclothed, without the splendour of the divine image and robbed of the Spirit's abundant grace; no longer shall we lament our old nakedness and say: 'I have taken off my tunic; how shall I put it on?' (Song of Songs 5:3). For in this paradise the serpent found no way in, the serpent whose false offer of godhead we craved (Genesis 3:5), and so were likened to the senseless beasts (Psalm 49:12). For the only-begotten Son of God himself, being God and of one being with the Father, formed himself into a man from this Virgin, this pure soil. And I, a man, have been made divine; I, a mortal, have been made immortal; and I have put off the garments of skin (Genesis 3:21). For I have stripped off corruption, and I am clothed in the robe of the Godhead. Today the Virgin, undefiled, who had no part in earthly passions but was nourished on heavenly thoughts, has not gone away into the earth; having become in truth a living heaven, she takes up her home in the heavenly tabernacles. For who would miss the truth in calling her heaven, unless perhaps someone, knowing well, should say that she is raised even above the heavens by a surpassing that admits no comparison? For the Maker and Sustainer of the heavens, the Craftsman of every work of creation within the world and beyond it, visible and invisible, he for whom nothing in all creation is a place (if indeed a place is defined as what contains the things in it), in her was fashioned by himself, without seed, into an infant; and he showed her to be a spacious storehouse of his Godhead, which fills all things and alone is uncircumscribed. He was wholly gathered into her without suffering, and remained wholly outside, being his own place, which nothing can contain. Today the treasure of life, the abyss of grace (I do not know how to say it with bold and fearless lips) is covered by a death that bears life; and she who conceived the destroyer of death approaches it without fear, if indeed we must call her all-holy and life-giving departure a death. For how could she who poured out true life for all fall under the power of death? But she yields to the law laid down by her own Son, and as daughter of the old Adam she undergoes the liability that came down from her father, since even her Son, who is Life itself, did not refuse it; but because she is Mother of the living God, she is fittingly carried over to him. For if God says, 'Lest the first-formed man stretch out his hand and take of the tree of life and taste it, and live forever' (Genesis 3:22), how shall she who received Life itself, without beginning and without end, bound by no limit of beginning or of end, not live for the age that has no end?

choices.note: Psalm renumbering: printed margin Ps 48:13 LXX = Psalm 49:12 in English numbering (the refrain recurs at 49:20).
Song of Songs 5:3 and Genesis 3:22 are printed in the margin;

Genesis 8:9 (the dove found rest for her feet) is a clear allusion; 2 Samuel 6:14-16 (David leaping before the ark) is cited because 'σκιρτᾷ Δαβίδ' stands beside the ark image (LXX 2 Kingdoms 6:16; compare 1 Chronicles 15:29);
Genesis 3:5 cited for the serpent's 'false deification' ('you will be like gods');
Genesis 3:21 for the garments of skin.

Doubtful readings: (1) printed 'ἐνδέδυμαι' in 'τοὺς δερματίνους χιτῶνας ἐνδέδυμαι' (checked at 600 dpi); rendered 'I have put off', following the sense of the context (deified, made immortal, stripped of corruption), which suggests ἐκδέδυμαι; if the printed text stands, the clause would read 'I have put on the garments of skin', which contradicts the following sentence.
(2) printed 'ὑπερέρχεται' ('passes beyond'); rendered 'undergoes' (ὑπέρχεται), since the next clause says her Son did not refuse these liabilities.
(3) printed 'ἀχειροτμήτῳ' ('not cut by hand'); rendered 'not made by hands' (sense of ἀχειροποιήτῳ; possible echo of Hebrews 9:11 or Mark 14:58, left uncited).
'λογικὸν παράδεισον' rendered 'the paradise endowed with reason' (Mary as the living paradise).
'νοητὸν κόσμον' rendered 'the world known to the mind'.
'τὰς πατρικὰς εὐθύνας' rendered 'the liability that came down from her father' (Adam).
'τόπον ἔχων ἑαυτοῦ ἀπερίληπτον' rendered 'being his own place, which nothing can contain'.
'τῷ τοῦ οἰκείου τόκου θεσμοθετήματι' rendered 'the law laid down by her own Son' (τόκος = offspring).
Apparatus readings not adopted: fn28 παραγίνεται; fn29 αὐτῷ ἄγγελοι; fn30 Colb.
νοητόν for λογικόν; fn31 ὁμιλήσασα; fn32 τῷ / τό; fn33 ἑαυτόν; fn34 ἀνακομίζεται (same sense).

Review: the facing Latin of PG 96 col. 726 supports both emendations: 'pelliceasque tunicas exui' (I have put off the garments of skin) and 'paternam sententiam subit' (undergoes the paternal sentence); it also joins 'robbed of the Spirit's grace' to the description of our former state ('uberrimaque Spiritus gratia spoliati'), as now rendered, so the English no longer implies we are still robbed.
Perfect tenses in the Eden clause rendered as perfects.
